items.readable_text:
Content:
Recall, previously, we saw how to express second-order and third-order homogeneous ODEs as a system of first-order differential equations. We use the same method for second-order and third-order inhomogeneous ODEs.

Content:
For instance, consider the third-order inhomogeneous differential equation
[MATH: y''' + 5y'' - 4y' + t^2y = t+1.]

Content:
We write this equation as a system of first-order differential equations using the following change of variables:
[MATH: x_{1}(t)|= y; x_{2}(t)|= y^{′}; x_{3}(t)|= y^{″}]

Content:
Differentiating the above equations with respect to [MATH: t,] we get
[MATH: x_{1}^{′}(t)|= y^{′}; x_{2}^{′}(t)|= y^{″}; x_{3}^{′}(t)|= y^{‴}]
which we can rewrite as
[MATH: {x_{1}^{′} = x_{2}; x_{2}^{′} = x_{3}; x_{3}^{′} = y^{‴}.]

Content:
At this point, we're almost done. We just need to write the right-hand side of the last equation in terms of [MATH: x_1,] [MATH: x_2,] and [MATH: x_3.]

Content:
Solving our original differential equation for the highest-order derivative [MATH: (y'''),] we obtain
[MATH: y''' = -5y'' + 4y' - t^2y + t + 1.]

Content:
Then, we substitute our new variables into the right-hand side of the above equation. This gives
[MATH: y''' = -5x_3 + 4x_2 - t^2x_1 + t + 1.]

Content:
Notice that we do not include any derivative terms on the right-hand side.

Content:
Therefore, our complete system of equations is as follows:
[MATH: {x_{1}^{′} = x_{2}; x_{2}^{′} = x_{3}; x_{3}^{′} = − 5x_{3} + 4x_{2} − t^{2}x_{1} + t + 1]

The second-order differential equation
[MATH: y'' - 7t y' + e^{t}y= -t]
can be written as a system of first-order differential equations, as follows:
[MATH: {x_{1}^{′} = x_{2}; x_{2}^{′} = f(t)]
where [MATH: x_1(t) = y(t)] and [MATH: x_2(t) = y'(t).] Find the function [MATH: f(t).]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
First, we make the following change of variables: [MATH: x_{1}(t)|= y; x_{2}(t)|= y^{′}]

Differentiating the above equations with respect to [MATH: t,] we get [MATH: x_{1}^{′}(t)|= y^{′}; x_{2}^{′}(t)|= y^{″}]

which we can rewrite as [MATH: {x_{1}^{′} = x_{2},; x_{2}^{′} = y^{″}.]

At this point, we're almost done. We just need to write the right-hand side of the last equation in terms of [MATH: x_1] and [MATH: x_2.]

Solving our original differential equation for the highest-order derivative [MATH: (y''),] we obtain [MATH: y'' = 7t y' - e^{t}y - t.]

Then, we substitute our new variables into the right-hand side of the above equation. This gives [MATH: y'' = 7t x_2 -e^{t}x_1 - t.] Notice that we do not include any derivative terms on the right-hand side.

Therefore, our complete system of equations is as follows: [MATH: {x_{1}^{′} = x_{2}; x_{2}^{′} = 7tx_{2} − e^{t}x_{1} − t]

Finally, [MATH: f(t) = -e^{t}x_1 + 7t x_2 - t.]

Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction
